audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Mel, Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Mel, Tryndamere, Tryndamere and contradicted its own whys at four stages: whys[2] says 'you poke, root and disengage anything a pre-Fury Trynd tries' under a Tryndamere label, whys[3] says 'Even window' under Tryndamere, whys[4] says 'Even at 6' under a Mel 7/10, and Mel reclaiming Level 6 after losing Levels 3-5 to a scaling crit champion is a power shift that never happens.
audit.why: Mel is 550 range with a 950 Q and a 1000 E against a melee with no gap-close until Spinning Slash at level 3 — the first three stages are hers. Fury and Spinning Slash even it out at 4-6, and first crit items hand it over for good. The packet levelChart already reads Mel, Mel, Mel, Skill, Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, which is exactly what the whys describe.
audit.corrected: Chart is now Mel, Mel, Mel, Skill, Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side, with ratings 7, 7, 6, 5, 5, 4, 3 so they descend monotonically instead of bouncing. No mirror file exists (audits/top/tryndamere__mel.json), so this side sets the direction.

audit.whatIsWrong: early said 'Levels 1-3 are yours because Trynd has no E yet' and spikes[0] labelled Lvl 2-3 as a window against 'a Trynd who has no E yet to escape'.
audit.why: Spinning Slash is available at level 3, so the free window is levels 1-2. Telling a 550-range mage that level 3 is still safe walks her into a 650-range gap-close on 12s at rank 1 — the exact spike the page was trying to warn about.
audit.corrected: The free window is now levels 1-2, and the spike says Spinning Slash comes online at 3 with its 650 range and 12/11/10/9/8 cooldown named.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout appears nowhere in either layer, and early instead spent a sentence saying 'he has no projectile to eat' — a non-interaction.
audit.why: Riot's text: Mocking Shout 'lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' It reaches 850 on 14s, further than Mel's 550 auto range, and the slow is conditional on facing away. That is the decisive kiting rule of the matchup and it is directly actionable: back off facing him and the slow does not apply. The page's advice to 'kite back out of crit range' was telling the player to do the one thing that triggers it.
audit.corrected: mid and wants.foe now carry the back-turned condition; the non-interaction sentence is replaced with Rebuttal's actual value here, which is that it prevents damage outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns, tradeBad and dontsFull[2].d carried no real numbers, and 'gone for twenty seconds' understates Rebuttal.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s. Undying Rage is 120/100/80. Spinning Slash is 12/11/10/9/8 at 650 range — that last one is the number that decides when Mel may step up, and it appeared nowhere.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns and ranges written into breakdown.cooldowns, tradeBad and dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, although the full layer's itemization line already says to add anti-heal.
audit.why: Bloodlust consumes Fury to heal, so every extended trade refunds the poke Mel just spent mana on. The _missing file flags this matchup specifically for anti-heal timing.
audit.corrected: late now names Morellonomicon against Bloodlust.

edits.before: Q + Solar Snare root is your cleanest punish — root him as he steps to last-hit and rain Radiant Volley on a Trynd who has no E yet to escape.
edits.after: Q plus Solar Snare's root is your cleanest punish — root him as he steps to last-hit and rain Radiant Volley before Spinning Slash comes online at 3.

edits.before: His threat window — full crit Trynd E-gaps your 550 range, spins through your one root, and survives your execute with Undying Rage; you cannot 1v1 him.
edits.after: His threat window — full-crit Trynd closes 650 with Spinning Slash, refunds your chip with Bloodlust, and survives your execute with Undying Rage.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours because Trynd has no E yet — he can only walk at you. Use Radiant Volley to poke him off the wave and the moment he steps up to last-hit, throw Solar Snare to root him and stack Overwhelm through the field's slow. Hold Rebuttal's barrier ready; he has no projectile to eat, so save the shield and move speed to body-block his step-in rather than wasting it. Do not push the wave — a shoved lane lets him E in on a gank or freely build Fury.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours because Spinning Slash is not up yet — he can only walk at you. Use Radiant Volley to poke him off the wave and the moment he steps up to last-hit, throw Solar Snare to root him and stack Overwhelm through the field's slow. Hold Rebuttal for the crit burst, not for chip: it prevents damage outright, which is the only thing that blanks a spin. Do not push the wave — a shoved lane lets him Spinning Slash in on a gank or bank Fury freely.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 tip toward even as his Fury and E come online. Your Q is ranking up and Overwhelm is accumulating, so keep poking, but respect that one E-spin puts him inside your range with no dash for you to answer. The trap at 6 is his Undying Rage: do NOT fire Golden Eclipse into a Trynd you cannot kill outright, because he survives at 1 HP for 5 full seconds and spins on you while your R is wasted. Land Solar Snare on his engage, kite with Rebuttal, and only detonate when he is already low and his R is on cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 tip toward even as Battle Fury and Spinning Slash (650 range, 12s at rank 1) come online. Your Q is ranking up and Overwhelm accumulating, so keep poking, but one spin puts him inside your range with no dash for you to answer. Mocking Shout only slows you if your back is turned, so retreat facing him. The trap at 6 is Undying Rage: do NOT fire Golden Eclipse into a Trynd you cannot kill outright. Root his engage, kite with Rebuttal, detonate once his R is down.

edits.before: This is where he takes over. A full-crit Tryndamere E-gaps past your 550 poke, spins through your single root, and shrugs off your execute with Undying Rage — you physically cannot win the straight 1v1. Stop dueling: shove and roam, hit other lanes with R from range, and never get caught alone in a side lane where he can run you down. Your scaling passive keeps you relevant in teamfights where you peel yourself with Solar Snare and let your frontline soak his spin, but the solo kill belongs to him now.
edits.after: This is where he takes over. A full-crit Tryndamere closes your 550 poke with Spinning Slash and shrugs off your execute with Undying Rage, while Bloodlust converts banked Fury straight back into health — buy Morellonomicon or the chip means nothing. Stop dueling: shove and roam, hit other lanes with R from range, and never get caught alone in a side lane. In teamfights peel yourself with Solar Snare and let your frontline soak the spin, but the solo kill belongs to him now.

notes: Kit flag misfire: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json tags Mocking Shout (W) with 'projectile', but Riot's own description is 'lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage' — a point-blank aura, not a projectile. Per the flag-versus-description rule I trusted the description and made no reflect claim about it in either direction. I also deleted the page's opposite assertion ('he has no projectile to eat'), which was both a non-interaction and unverifiable. Left alone as unverified: the '1 HP for 5s' figure for Undying Rage that spikes[1] and whys[4] both use — Riot's text gives no duration and the kit file has no number, so I did not touch it. Also unverified and therefore not written: whether Spinning Slash's cooldown is reduced by critical strikes. Packet reports games:null for tryndamere while MC_REAL_GAMES.mel.tryndamere is 1014 — packet build defect.
